price_value.rationale: At $24,995 it sits above the fair-value range of $14,747–$22,333 (mid $17,002). The claimed new OME suspension, tires, wheels and timing belt explain part of the premium, but none is documented. The reported accident should pull price down, not up.

mission_fit.rationale: It offers body-on-frame V8 4WD, a roof rack for a rooftop tent and cargo room for a sleeping platform, which the RX lacks. The build is mild rather than hard-core. It overlaps the RX as a family hauler and is justified only if that capability is wanted.

logistics.rationale: The car is at a San Diego dealer, 372 mi away, within CA, with the dealer responsible for smog. A PPI at a nearby Toyota/Lexus independent shop should be arrangeable but is not yet confirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Ash Grey is a desirable colour, and OME suspension on TRD Pro wheels is a tasteful, coherent mild build. It is otherwise a typical GX470 with no Sport Package noted.

seller_questions: Can you send the full Carfax or AutoCheck, including the accident entry's date, damage area and severity?
Can you provide the invoice for the timing belt and water pump, showing date, odometer and parts brand (Aisin/OEM)? Were the idlers, tensioner and thermostat also replaced?
Which OME MT64 part numbers were installed front and rear? Is there an invoice and an alignment printout?
How was the rear air suspension deleted (coils and compressor disabled, height sensor handled)? Does the height-control or VSC light stay off?
Has the radiator ever been replaced, and when? Is it still the OEM plastic-tank unit?
Can you send photos of the frame rails, rear crossmember and underbody, including the area repaired after the reported accident?
What are the DOT date codes on the four KO3 tires?
When were the transfer case, front/rear differential and transmission fluids last serviced?
Have the lower ball joints been replaced under the recall or since?
Will you allow an independent PPI at a nearby Toyota/Lexus shop before any deposit, and can you send a cold-start video?
Can you provide the smog certificate and confirm the title is clean, not branded?
ppi_focus: Frame and body: look for accident-repair evidence (weld marks, overspray, panel gaps, frame straightness) and any rust.
Cooling system: radiator tanks, hoses, water pump weep, coolant condition; pressure test.
Timing belt: inspect the cover or look for a dated sticker to confirm recent replacement.
Suspension: OME install quality, rear coil conversion, UCA/ball-joint angles with the lift, alignment within spec, CV boots.
Scan all modules: height control, VSC/ABS, secondary air injection, pending codes.
Exhaust manifolds: check for cracks or cold-start tick.
Transfer case, differential and transmission fluid condition and leaks; rear main and valve cover seepage.
Tire date codes and uniform wear; brake condition to confirm the claimed new pads and rotors.
Dashboard: confirm the replaced dash (recall) has no cracks; check the roof rack mounts for rooftop-tent suitability.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: invoices for the timing belt/water pump and suspension work, plus a history report showing a minor, properly repaired accident with a clean title.
Up: a clean PPI with a straight, rust-free frame, no warning lights and a replaced radiator.
Up: a price negotiated toward the upper fair-value band.
Down: a structural or frame-involved accident, a branded title, or refusal to allow a PPI.
Down: a height-control light or a poorly executed air-suspension delete, cooling-system issues, or a failed smog check.
evidence.mission_note: A GX470 with a mild OME build and roof rack supplies body-on-frame 4WD and rooftop-tent/sleeping-platform capability the RX 350 lacks. It fits the capability branch only if that capability is actually wanted, and it overlaps the RX otherwise.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity (a VIN decoding as a 2006 GX 470 V8) and all-fees-included terms at $24,995, above the $14,747–$22,333 fair-value range. The history-report summary shows an accident or damage event and multiple owners, with no repair documentation. The dealer claims a broad refresh: timing belt, water pump, CV axles, sway links, brakes and rotors, new OME MT64 suspension with the air bags deleted, and new KO3 tires. None of it is supported by invoices. Only the first attached photo appears to be this car; it shows a clean gray exterior, a mild lift and fresh matching all-terrains. The other photos depict different vehicles and give no evidence about this one. Frame and underbody condition, radiator and cooling history, warning-light status after the air delete, and title status all remain open.
evidence.next_action: Ask Miramar Motorsports for the full history report detailing the accident, the timing belt and suspension invoices, tire date codes and underbody photos. Then book an independent PPI near San Diego before any deposit.
